prerequisites: Knowledge and abilities in all topics of Radio-link technologies

learning_outcomes.text: Understand and analyze systems and services that rely on electromagnetic fields and connect the properties and behavior of the fields to the physical structures they interact with.
Develop initial skills necessary to design or integrate electromagnetic field-based systems into more complex systems.
Students must know the properties of electromagnetic fields and the main devices that use them.
Be able to correctly evaluate the effects of electromagnetic phenomena on the behavior of ICT (and, more generally, electronic) equipment.
Apply standard solutions to different cases and evaluate their feasibility.
Build an appropriate model of a physical situation, solve it, and interpret the mathematical solutions found.
Deal with the study, integration, and design of equipment, systems, and services that use electromagnetic fields.
Interact efficiently with the designers of electromagnetic devices.

syllabus_topics: Real transmission lines and matching structures
Dielectric behavior and propagation at RF and microwaves
Theorems of reciprocity, uniqueness and equivalence
assessment_rules: The final verification consists of a written part (maximum 14 points) and an oral exam (maximum 20 points). To pass, a student must get a minimum of 5 points in the written part and a minimum of 12 points in the oral part. The sum of the two partial marks must be at least 18. For specific didactic needs related to the epidemiological situation, either the written test or the oral part or both can be held at a distance, with possible adjustments to maximum and minimum scores.
